title: Precomposition is the dual mate for the finite-frame pairing
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $P,R$ be bounded cochain complexes of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Put $B^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(B,A[0])$ for $B=P,R$, with differential $(d^\vee\varphi)(x)=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(dx)$ in degree $j$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Use the total tensor differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with the canonical associators and unitors. For each $B=P,R$ and integer $i$, choose a finite dual frame $(e^B_{i,a},\epsilon^B_{i,a})_a$ satisfying $x=\sum_a e^B_{i,a}\epsilon^B_{i,a}(x)$, empty when $B^i=0$. Let $\operatorname{ev}_B:B^\vee\otimes B\to A[0]$ and $\operatorname{coev}_B:A[0]\to B\otimes B^\vee$ be the graded maps given by evaluation (zero off total degree zero) and $\operatorname{coev}_B(1)=\sum_{i,a}e^B_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon^B_{i,a}$. Assume these maps are chain maps and satisfy the two triangle identities. For every degree-zero chain map $f:P\to R$, precomposition $f^\vee:R^\vee\to P^\vee$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi f$, is the unique chain map $u:R^\vee\to P^\vee$ for which
$$\operatorname{ev}_P\circ(u\otimes1_P)=\operatorname{ev}_R\circ(1_{R^\vee}\otimes f).$$
It also satisfies the coevaluation identity
$$(f\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ\operatorname{coev}_P=(1_R\otimes f^\vee)\circ\operatorname{coev}_R.$$
Thus the explicit precomposition map is the right dual mate for these chosen pairings.

proof.text:
For a homogeneous \(\varphi\in R^\vee\) of degree \(j\) and \(x\in P^{-j-1}\), the dual differential gives
\[
(d_P^\vee(f^\vee\varphi))(x)=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(f(d_Px))=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(d_R(fx))=((d_R^\vee\varphi)\circ f)(x).
\]
The middle equality is the chain-map identity for \(f\). Both sides vanish on the other degrees by the grading conventions. Thus precomposition \(f^\vee(\varphi)=\varphi\circ f\) is a degree-zero chain map \(R^\vee\to P^\vee\).

source.place: Final two sentences: identifying the maps on duals when transporting the frame duality along an isomorphism.

proof.text:
On a homogeneous pure tensor \(\varphi\otimes x\) with \(\varphi\in(R^\vee)^j\) and \(x\in P^{-j}\), the two composites in the evaluation equation both have value \(\varphi(fx)\): the left side is \(\operatorname{ev}_P((f^\vee\varphi)\otimes x)\) and the right side is \(\operatorname{ev}_R(\varphi\otimes f(x))\). On all other total degrees both evaluations are zero by definition. Since pure tensors generate the tensor product and the canonical associators and unitors only reparenthesize them, this proves
\[
\operatorname{ev}_P\circ(f^\vee\otimes1_P)=\operatorname{ev}_R\circ(1_{R^\vee}\otimes f).
\]

source.place: Final two sentences: identifying the maps on duals when transporting the frame duality along an isomorphism.

proof.text: If a degree-zero chain map \(u:R^\vee\to P^\vee\) satisfies the displayed evaluation equation, then for every homogeneous \(\varphi\in(R^\vee)^j\) and every \(x\in P^{-j}\) it gives \((u\varphi)(x)=\varphi(fx)\). Thus \(u\varphi\) and \(f^\vee\varphi\) agree on all of \(P^{-j}\), hence are equal as degree-\(j\) functionals. This holds in every degree, so \(u=f^\vee\); the precomposition map is the unique chain map with the mate property.

proof.text:
Write the chosen frames as \((e^P_{i,a},\epsilon^P_{i,a})\) and \((e^R_{k,b},\epsilon^R_{k,b})\). Evaluating the left side of the coevaluation identity at \(1\) and expanding each \(f(e^P_{i,a})\) in the \(R^i\)-frame gives
\[
\sum_{i,a,b}e^R_{i,b}\,\epsilon^R_{i,b}(f(e^P_{i,a}))\otimes\epsilon^P_{i,a}.
\]
For the right side, expand each functional \(\epsilon^R_{i,b}\circ f\) in the \(P^i\)-frame; the frame identity gives
\[
\epsilon^R_{i,b}\circ f=\sum_a\epsilon^R_{i,b}(f(e^P_{i,a}))\,\epsilon^P_{i,a}.
\]
Therefore its value at \(1\) is the same finite sum. Since both maps have source \(A[0]\), equality at \(1\) proves
\[
(f\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ\operatorname{coev}_P=(1_R\otimes f^\vee)\circ\operatorname{coev}_R.
\]
